title: Landscaping Quote Excavation Line Item: What Barrie Homeowners Should Demand
seoTitle: Landscaping Quote Excavation Barrie: Why It Matters
seoDescription: A Barrie landscaping quote without an excavation line item hides the 30-40% of the budget that actually determines whether your patio survives freeze-thaw.
tldr: A proper Barrie landscaping quote should show excavation as its own line item, typically 25-40% of the total hardscape cost. Excavation covers digging out 30-45cm of native clay, hauling it away, and prepping for the base. When it is buried inside a lump-sum price, you cannot tell whether the contractor dug deep enough to survive Barrie freeze-thaw cycles — and a shallow dig is the number-one reason patios heave within three winters.
intro:
Here is the thing nobody tells you when you collect three quotes for a paver patio in Barrie: the two-page proposal that just says Supply and install 400 sq ft paver patio — $18,000 is hiding the most important part of the job. Excavation and base prep is 25-40% of what you are paying for, and it is the single part of the build that determines whether your patio is flat in ten years or cracked and heaved in three.

We dig on Barrie clay every week. The soil around Bayfield Street, Ardagh, and out toward Innisfil is heavy, water-holding clay that swells when it freezes and shrinks when it dries. If a contractor does not remove enough of it and replace it with a proper compacted stone base, the ground does the moving and your stonework goes along for the ride.

A quote that buries excavation in a single lump-sum number is not being generous with you — it is protecting itself. When it is a separate line, you can see exactly what you are buying underground, where 90% of failures actually happen.

sections.heading: What does the excavation line item actually pay for?
sections.html:
Excavation on a Barrie hardscape job is not just digging a hole. A single line labelled excavation should cover four distinct pieces of work, and a decent contractor will tell you which ones are included when you ask.

  • Cutting to grade: removing 30-45cm of native clay across the full footprint, plus a 15cm over-dig past the finished edge so the base is supported under the pavers, not just beside them.
  • Spoil removal: a 400 sq ft patio dug to 40cm generates roughly 18-22 cubic metres of wet clay. That is 3-4 dump trailer loads that have to be hauled off-site and dumped — a real cost, often $600-$1,200 on its own.
  • Machine and access: a mini-excavator or skid steer, the operator, float delivery, and any hand-digging around a gas line or a Bell pedestal.
  • Sub-grade compaction: compacting the exposed clay before a single scoop of stone goes in.

On most residential jobs in Simcoe County, excavation and disposal land between $8 and $16 per square foot depending on dig depth, soil wetness, and how far the machine has to travel from the driveway to the work. If your quote does not break this out, you have no way to compare one bidder's underground work against another's — you are only comparing the pretty part on top. This is exactly the kind of buried number we flag in the hidden costs of cheap landscaping.

sections.heading: Why does dig depth matter so much in Barrie clay?
sections.html:
Dig depth matters in Barrie because our frost line reaches roughly 1.2 metres and our clay soil holds water, so any base that is too shallow will heave every single winter. Freeze-thaw is not a once-a-season event here — Barrie routinely swings above and below 0°C dozens of times between November and April, and each cycle expands and contracts the ground.

The physics is simple: water-saturated clay expands about 9% when it freezes. If your pavers sit on 8cm of stone over undisturbed clay, that clay lifts the whole assembly unevenly. Corners rise, joints open, and by the third spring you have a patio that pools water and rocks underfoot.

Golden Maple builds on a 12-16 inch (30-40cm) compacted clear-stone base — not granular A. Clear stone (19mm angular washed stone) drains freely and does not trap the water that fuels frost heave the way granular A's fines do. But you only get a 16-inch base if the excavation went 16 inches deep plus the paver and bedding thickness. That is why depth belongs on the quote in writing: it is the difference between a base spec and a base promise. If you want to understand how base depth and other build decisions drive the final number, the project cost estimator walks through it.

sections.heading: How can you spot a lowball quote that skimped on excavation?
sections.html:
You spot a skimped excavation by comparing the dig depth and disposal volume across quotes — the cheap bid almost always cut them, not the pavers. Two quotes can name the same Techo-Bloc or Unilock paver and be $6,000 apart, and the gap is almost never the stone on top. It is the stone and labour underneath.

Here is what a lowballer quietly removes to hit a headline price:

  • Shallow dig: 15-20cm instead of 30-40cm. Half the excavation cost, half the base, double the heave risk.
  • Granular A instead of clear stone: cheaper per tonne and packs faster, but its fines hold water — the enemy in a freeze-thaw climate.
  • No spoil removal: the dug clay gets spread across your yard or left in a pile you now have to deal with.
  • No over-dig at the edges: so the perimeter — the first thing to fail — has no base support.

When one Barrie quote is 30% cheaper than the others, ask each contractor a single question: how deep are you digging and how many loads are you hauling? The honest answer sorts them fast. We cover the full vetting process in our guide to choosing a landscaping contractor in Barrie.

sections.heading: What should a proper excavation line item look like on paper?
sections.html:
A proper excavation line reads like a spec, not a slogan. It states depth in centimetres or inches, names the base material, and accounts for hauling the spoil away. Vague language is the tell — prep site as required could mean anything, and legally it means whatever is cheapest for the contractor.

Compare these two ways of writing the same line on a 400 sq ft patio:

  • Weak: Excavation and grading — included.
  • Strong: Excavate 400 sq ft to 45cm depth including 15cm over-dig at perimeter; haul and dispose approx. 20 m³ native clay; compact sub-grade; install and compact 35cm clear-stone base in 10cm lifts — $6,400.

The strong version tells you the depth (45cm), the material (clear stone), the compaction method (10cm lifts, which matters because a base compacted in one thick layer never reaches density), and the disposal volume. It also gives you a number you can hold the contractor to. Golden Maple sources base stone from Carr Landscape Depot in Barrie, so the material spec on our quotes matches what actually gets delivered to your driveway. If you want to see how that base translates into a finished surface, our project portfolio shows completed Simcoe County installs.

sections.heading: Does a permit or bylaw ever affect the excavation line?
sections.html:
Yes — City of Barrie bylaws can affect excavation cost and depth, particularly for grading near a property line, work over a registered easement, or anything that changes drainage onto a neighbour's lot. A quote that ignores this is a quote that has not walked your specific site.

A few Barrie-specific realities that belong in the excavation conversation:

  • Locate before you dig: Ontario One Call locates for gas, hydro, and Bell are mandatory and free, but they take up to 5 business days. A contractor who plans to dig tomorrow has not called them.
  • Drainage and grading: Barrie's lot-grading rules mean water cannot be redirected onto a neighbouring property. Excavation depth and slope on a patio near the lot line can trigger this.
  • Retaining structures: a wall over 1 metre high in many Simcoe County municipalities needs engineering, which changes the excavation footprint and cost.

None of this is meant to scare you — it is meant to show why a real quote comes after a site visit, not off a phone call. When the excavation line reflects your actual clay, your actual slope, and your actual access from the driveway, you are looking at a price that will hold. The lowball that skipped the site visit is a number that will grow the day the machine arrives. Reach out through our contact page and we will walk the site before we quote a metre of it.

faqs.question: how much is excavation in a landscaping quote in Barrie
faqs.answer: Excavation and disposal typically run $8-$16 per square foot on a Barrie hardscape job, or roughly 25-40% of the total. The range depends on dig depth, how wet the clay is, and how far the machine has to travel from the driveway to the work area.

faqs.question: why is one landscaping quote so much cheaper than the others
faqs.answer: The cheapest quote almost always skimped underground, not on the pavers. Common cuts are a shallower dig (15-20cm instead of 30-40cm), cheaper granular A base instead of clear stone, and no spoil removal. Ask each contractor how deep they dig and how many loads they haul — the honest answer sorts them out.

faqs.question: how deep should a patio be excavated in Ontario
faqs.answer: For a Barrie-area patio, plan on 30-45cm of excavation to fit a 12-16 inch compacted stone base plus bedding and paver thickness. Depth matters because our frost line reaches about 1.2 metres and clay soil heaves with every freeze-thaw cycle when the base is too shallow.

faqs.question: what is the difference between clear stone and granular A for a paver base
faqs.answer: Clear stone is washed 19mm angular stone with no fines, so it drains freely and resists frost heave. Granular A contains fine particles that pack tighter but trap water — a problem in Barrie's water-holding clay. Golden Maple builds on clear stone specifically for this freeze-thaw climate.

faqs.question: should excavation be a separate line on a landscaping quote
faqs.answer: Yes. Excavation is 25-40% of a hardscape budget and it is where most failures start, so it belongs on its own line stating depth, base material, and disposal volume. A lump-sum quote that hides it gives you no way to compare the underground work that actually determines whether the project lasts.

faqs.question: do I need a permit to excavate for a patio in Barrie
faqs.answer: A standard grade-level patio usually does not need a building permit, but City of Barrie lot-grading rules apply if excavation changes drainage toward a neighbour, and retaining walls over 1 metre often require engineering. Mandatory Ontario One Call utility locates take up to 5 business days before any dig.

faqs.question: what happens if a contractor does not dig deep enough for my patio
faqs.answer: A shallow dig leaves your pavers sitting on native clay that freezes and swells about 9% each winter, lifting corners and opening joints. In Barrie's climate this typically shows up as visible heaving and pooling water within two to three winters, and the only real fix is tearing it out and rebuilding the base.
